speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Education for each year in the past five years (a) what is the number of teacher counsellors employed in schools in Singapore; (b) what is the average percentage of teachers who are teacher counsellors in each school; and (c) how many hours of counselling training do these teachers undergo.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Working together, they provide a caring environment for our students to grow and thrive.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
text: For all students, in addition to imparting academic content, teachers impart important habits and skills to strengthen our students' socio-emotional well-being and resilience.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
text: This is done through lessons and regular interactions with students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Among teachers, form teachers play a key role in supporting students' well-being and growth through building a positive class community.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Schools have also put in place peer support networks to enable students to offer socio-emotional support to one another.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Students who require more specialised counselling support are attended to by trained school counsellors beyond the peer support and teacher counsellor support frameworks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Students who require more specialised interventions are referred to health professionals and community resources like REACH and Family Service Centres.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
text: We also believe that parents play a key role in helping their children acquire self-management skills, take responsibility for their actions and bounce back from setbacks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
text: Schools will continue to work closely with parents to develop their children's social and emotional competencies, including through our Parent Support Groups.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think the Second Minister gave the number of teacher counsellors for all the schools.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But could I just ask for part (b) of my question on what percentage of teachers in each school are teacher counsellors?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Second, it is an important point that a lot of counsellors tell me that to be a counsellor, they require at least a Master's degree in counselling, because it is difficult work and requires specialised training.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, could I ask again whether we are setting our teachers up for failure by asking them to do even basic counselling work?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Second Minister mentioned maybe a one-day training; is there sufficient training for these teachers to be able to carry out this specialised work?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Third, it really is also what I have been pushing for.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Is it really needed for them to do this extra work, or could the Ministry of Education (MOE) set aside some funding to hire more school counsellors who are able to help the students better and essentially help the teachers as well?

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: So, it is hard to say what is the percentage across all the different schools.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: But suffice to say, first, I want to reiterate the distinction between school counsellors and teacher counsellors.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: The one that Mr Louis Ng talked about in terms of requiring specialised training, for example, Master's degree in counselling, they are our school counsellors.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: They are the ones who will do the real counselling work for the cases which are more complicated, more complex, that require more intervention.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: And most of the cases in schools are handled by the school counsellors.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: And the school counsellors do not do the teaching.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: But the question that Mr Ng asked is about teacher counsellors.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: The teacher counsellors augment the work of the school counsellors.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: And that is the reason why the training is on psychological first aid; they are the ones who help the less complex cases.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: They are the ones who, when the school or the class form teachers identify a student who is manifesting some challenges, they are referred to the teacher counsellors and the teacher counsellors will try to support and help them.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: So, the teacher counsellors are not expected to do the kind of counselling that require Master's level qualification.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: They are asked to support less complex cases.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: And when we talk about the teacher counsellors, I just want to highlight that when we identify the teachers, we do not just identify whoever that we think, "Oh, you should do it and the school needs these teachers".

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We identify teachers who are suitable and have interest.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: They, first, must have the interest to want to do more than just teaching and a predisposition to provide counselling, intervention support, as well as those with some prior counselling experience and training.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: There are some teachers who were former social workers.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: So, they already have got some training in counselling experience.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Some teachers who came from the social service sector do have some experience already and we ask them whether they are prepared to do so.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: So, they are teachers who have already had some background.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: They take on the role and they are very committed and we know they have done a lot of work.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: The school counsellors are the professionals who have been recruited by MOE to deal with the more challenging counselling cases.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Within the school system, as I have mentioned previously, we have structures and systems in place to ensure a manageable workload for all our staff.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: So, for example, teaching fewer classes or taking less co-curricular activities or committee duties.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: So, if you are a teacher counsellor, depending on how much counselling you are doing, you are off-loaded from other teaching duties; just to be fair to the teachers.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: And the school leaders are given the guideline within this framework to be able to help the teachers.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: So, besides implementing these off-loading provisions, school leaders also adopt a holistic approach in deploying teacher counsellors to ensure that their work is sustainable.
So, I want to assure Mr Louis Ng that we know the teachers have done a lot of work and they continue to do a lot of work.
We are fully aware of the amount of work they have put in.
Some have gone beyond the call of duty in doing so.
We will do our best within the school system and not every school is the same because the needs of the schools differ.
And with the framework and guidelines we have given the school leaders, we hope the school leaders will be able to be fair to all the teachers within the school manpower.

And we also hope that if teachers who feel that they are being loaded with more than what they can handle can go to the school staff developer in the school, talk to the school leaders and manage the workload within the construct of the team in the school.

speaker: Mr Speaker
